newsitem.title: UK: AIOC SELECTS BROWN AND ROOT FOR CASPIAN OIL.
newsitem.headline: AIOC SELECTS BROWN AND ROOT FOR CASPIAN OIL.

text.p: An $8 billion consortium has issued a letter of intent to award a services contract to Brown and Root to develop hydrocarbons in the Caspian Sea, a company statement said on Monday.

"The Azerbaijan International Operating Company (AIOC) has issued Brown and Root a letter of intent relating to the award of a contract to provide engineering design and procurement services for Phase I of the Guneshli Chirag Azeri (GCA) offshore fields in the Caspian Sea," the statement from Brown and Root said.
"We are proud to have been selected to continue to play an important role in developing Azerbaijan's oil and gas infrastructure," Brown and Root's regional Managing director Malcolm Dorricott said.

The development is likely to centre on a single processing platform as well as two drilling and wellhead platforms for up to 80 wells, and the facilities will be capable of producing 300,000 barrels per day (bpd.)

The company's involvement in the project will also include design and procurement activities for infield pipelines, main oil and gas pipelines to the Sangachal onshore terminal 200 km away and expansion of the onshore terminal.
It will also include upgrading existing export pipelines to the Russian Black Sea port of Novorossiisk and the Georgian Black Sea port of Supsa, the statement said, but gave no details.
The five countries bordering the Caspian sea are at loggerheads over ownership of oil prospects and Turkmenistan says it partially owns the Chirag field and fully owns the Azeri field.
But the AIOC, an $8 billion consortium led by British Petroleum Co Plc and Norway's Statoil, has said it is not unduly concerned about the dispute.
Brown and Root is a subsidiary of energy services firm Halliburton Co .
